For 1st Respondent : Mr.J.Vishnu  For R2 and R3 : Dispensed with  JUDGMENT This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed to set aside award passed in MCOP No.9 of 2016, dated 07/08/2019 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Theni.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.The facts in brief:-
On 14/08/2015 at about 02.00 am, the petitioner travelling in a Tourist Bus bearing registration No.PY-01-CJ-5999 from Theni to Chennai.
When the bus was nearing the place of occurrence, the driver of Bus hit a parked Lorry bearing registration No.TN-48-AB-4599.
As result of which, the driver of the Bus, died on the spot and another person by name Aravindhan.
The petitioners namely Dr.Amudhan and R.Muthuraj and one another were taken to Government Hospital, Perambalur.
3.Over the occurrence, a case in Crime No.404 of 2015 was registered by the Mangalamedu Police station for the offences under sections 279, 337, 337 and 304(A) IPC.
The petitioners filed separate petitions in MCOP Nos.262 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of 2015 and 9 of 2016 seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- and Rs.25,00,000/- respectively.

entities.text: MCOP Nos.262 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of 2015 and 9 of 2016
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Both were taken together.
3.That was resisted by the appellants herein stating that 3rd respondent vehicle driver parked the Lorry with proper indication; Only the first respondent vehicle driver without noticing the parked vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit the parked vehicle; As result of which, the occurrence took place.
4.Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants, 5 witnesses were examined and 27 documents were marked.
On the side of the Insurance Companies, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.

FIR copy was marked through the witness as Ex.X1.
5.At
the conclusion of the trial process
, the Tribunal, after considering the evidence on record recorded a finding that the occurrence took place because of the rash and negligent driving on the part of the both the vehicle drivers.
So, it fixed the negligence at 50:50 as composite negligence.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
6.Regarding the compensation, so far as MCOP No.9 of 2016 is concerned, which is the subject matter of this appeal, it assessed the disability at 30%.
There was fracture on his spinal chord.

sentences.text: 2 Considering the nature of the injuries suffered, the above said partial permanent disability was fixed.
Rs.3,000/- was taken as compensation for one percentage of disability.

Finally, the Tribunal arrived at the following figure as per the tabulation given hereunder:-
 Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/-
 30% disability Rs. 90,000/-

Medical expenses Rs.2,85,279/-
 Attendant charges Rs. 4,000/-

Transport charges Rs. 4,000/-
 Extra Nourishment Rs. 10,000/-
 Damages to clothes Rs. 2,000/-
 Total Rs.4,45,279/-
7.Against which, this appeal is filed.
8.Heard both sides.
9.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that only on the point of wrong findings of the Tribunal, this appeal is preferred.
He is referring to the medical bills under Exs.A17 and A18.
The total https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis amount is Rs.2,83,213/-.
That amount was claimed by the claimant from their Insurance Companies, which is also admitted by him.
But the Tribunal recorded a finding that in spite of the above said receipt, the claimant is entitled to claim compensation from the appellants.
10.There is no question of double compensation.
So that sort of finding of the Tribunal is set aside.
The medical bills under Exs.A17 and A18 to the tune of Rs. 2,85,279/- is deducted from the total compensation.

Accordingly, the claimant in MCOP No.9 of 2016 is entitled to the total compensation as per the recalculation made hereunder:-
Head
Amount
awarded
Amount awarded by by the Tribunal this court Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/- Rs. 50,000/- 30% disability Rs. 90,000/- Rs. 90,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.2,85,279/- Nil
Attendant charges Rs. 4,000/- Rs. 4,000/-
Transport charges Rs. 4,000/- Rs. 4,000/-

Extra Nourishment Rs. 10,000/- Rs.
10,000/- Damages to clothes Rs. 2,000/- Rs. 2,000/- Total Rs.4,45,279/-
Rs.2,85,279/-
11.Both appellants are directed to pay the modified compensation of Rs.2,85,279/- equally to the claimant as per the order of the Tribunal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
12.In the result
, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
The award of the Tribunal is modified as Rs.2,85,279/-.

No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
